reviews.title: A whole new appreciation for sleep and science
reviews.contents:
A few weeks ago I stumbled across rise. I have been using another sleep tracking app for years but it’s become more of an alarm with some data. 

As soon as I joined rise it used all of my sleep data to calculate how much sleep I need which takes into account when you have “rebound” sleep. You know those lazy sundays you finally let you body catch up!! I started with over 12 hours of sleep debt in the past two weeks, with a suggested bed time and “rise” wake up time I went to work on getting my sleep debt down, a few weeks better I can already feel much a difference in my day to day life like I’m no longer running on empty! Also learning about the body’s natural circadian rhythm during the day and how to align daily tasks to make the most out of your day. 

A great app to have in your toolbox to make the most out of your day and understand your unique sleep needs and to keep on top of them to feel your best!!

reviews.title: Doesn’t live up to expectations
reviews.contents:
I expected this app be amazing from the ads and the science it refers to. The quiz to determine your sleep issues also appealed. However I found the app a bit basic and really don’t offer that much value. The quiz is not overly comprehensive and didn’t give the option to include some of the critical factors affecting your sleep, like sleep apnea and children (it did give a sleep apnea option, but you could only choose ONE priority from a list). It told me i need to sleep 9 hours which is true, but the sleep window ideal for me it gave me is just not viable with small children. The app told me that I have a sleep debt but no solution for fixing it other than sleeping 9 hours + per day between certain hours. The energy level chart that supposedly give you “optimal” times, did not reflect how I felt. It’s also impossible to figure out how to cancel the alarm once it’s set.
I’m a paying customer of AutoSleep and that gives me more valuable info and actually helped me get diagnosed with sleep apnea. I don’t think this app would make any impact on my life so I decided not to pay for a subscription

reviews.title: Overall brilliant, some minor bugs
reviews.contents:
Very cool app that tracks your energy level! Compared to all other apps I’ve used, this is by far the most accurate and well designed.

There are some bugs tho, such as the notification sometimes not working mentioned in the other comments. But the most annoying one is that the app becomes kinda dodgy after 12am midnight, with widget not working, notification being sent that’s supposed to be for the next morning, energy page taking minutes to load etc.

Overall though very good app. For those complaining about being charged after the trial - that’s how App Store works and it’s not hard at all to cancel your trial before being charged.

reviews.title: Rise: Energy and Sleep Tracker
reviews.contents: I spent just over five minutes making an account and even longer reading all the information that the app was telling me just to find out I have to pay now I know that I should check before I download the app but I didn’t because I never get any sleep and can never wake up when I do get to sleep so I was trying to see if this app was any good. I’ve seen this app advertised on many different platforms non of them say I have to pay or they say this app is free. I feel they have falsely advertised this app and it has makes me frustrated. Thanks for the app creation I know how expensive and time consuming app making is but please make sure that people know that you have to pay before making a new account or give us a choice to just not pay and continue to use the app but with some limitations. By the way I hated writing this because I feel like the biggest of big Karen but I do feel this should be known to other people before wasting time and probably even data before downloading.

reviews.title: Automatically charges after trial ends.
reviews.contents:
Once your free trial ends you are automatically charged the $86 for a whole year subscription without any further correspondence or in-app notification. 
I’m not saying it’s not a good app, but for me the functionality is limited as i don’t wear any biometric monitoring devices such as Fitbit or Apple Watch. Would I have paid $86 for this? No that’s almost a whole days pay for me. Would I have paid $7.16 per month, cancel anytime? Yes I would have given it at least a few months to see if it helps adjust my sleep habits. Anyway I guess I have a full year to find out because I’m forgot to cancel my trial.  

Apple needs to change how subscriptions work. Users should upon opening an app with a trial be notified that the trial has expired, then have to agree to a subscription. The current model means if you forget to cancel your trial you can have $86 that you need for food and stuff be taken out of your account.

reviews.title: Useful, buggy, bad pricing practices
reviews.contents:
This is a useful app. It’s helpful for keeping track of sleep debt and working towards getting it down. 

It does seem to have numerous bugs. Notifications don’t work at all for me: not most iOS notifications, nor SMS, nor the email they said they would send before my subscription started.   I’ve checked all my settings and they’re fine—the notifications just don’t work. Also the iOS widgets come up with some weird numbers. The widget says my “evening peak” time is 2:25am–9:24pm. 

I’m not a fan of charging for the whole year at once. If Rise are confident in the ongoing usefulness of their product, why not offer a monthly subscription? Making it yearly just seems to be taking advantage of people who might forget to cancel their trial, or of people who decide it’s not for them after a couple of months’ use.

reviews.title: $86 to tell me my sleep debt
reviews.contents:
The app is overall right about sleep debt and how to feel better by catching up on it. It is a very expensive app with with features that go all-in on their idea of how to take advantage of your sleep cycle. You buy it for a sense of commitment to improving your sleep moreso than its actual features.

How are the features? Well every morning it tells me that I will be a bit groggy after I wake up, for an hour or so. Amazing. It tells me my energy levels in graph form, with “peaks and dips”, but I found it was just wrong most of the time. I’d often feel energetic when it told me I was in a dip, for example. It doesn’t know when I eat a big lunch or when I have a coffee or if I forgot to drink water that day, and things like that affect me a lot. So it’s hard to say whether the graph is right, or whether it’s like a broken clock. But most of the time when I look at it my response is “wait, what?”

I think if you have a particularly troubled relationship with sleep, this app may be worth the money, but otherwise it really really isn’t. I paid $86 for a year of being able to look at a number (sleep debt) and go “yeah, that sounds about right”. That’s all the value I got out of it. It’s priced similarly to a years subscription to Microsoft Office 365, for a reference point.

I think a more effective use of your $86 would be to put it towards a cheap Fitbit or something so that you get a more holistic view of your energy levels, including how exercise and lack of sleep affects you. This app has some cool research behind it but honestly I feel like these features should be built into a bigger service, like Fitbit or Apple Health, rather than being something you pay for on their own.

reviews.title: It’s alright
reviews.contents:
The app itself does seem good, and well designed, and I did enjoy it, but didn’t really need it and eventually got busy and forgot about the app.

One problem though, I started the free trial and I believe the app was supposed to send me notifications before I started paying for it. After a while I forgot completely about it since I never got any notifications, and when I’d check my iPhone subscription s where everything shoulder come up it wasn’t there, so normally I assumed i already cancelled it.

I found out later I had in fact not cancelled it when money was taken out of my account, that’s when I went on the app and then realised I was still apparently subscribed to it.

I understand it is my fault for forgetting if I unsubscribed or not but when I’m relying on all my subscriptions to be in my settings since I don’t have time to go through every app I have, and the Rise subscription isn’t there but rather in the app when you go to the specific section it can get pretty annoying. I’m not sure if this is programmed with the app or it is my phone that is at fault, either way future downloaders on IPhone just make sure you don’t make the same mistake I did and forget.

reviews.title: Drains my battery
reviews.contents:
Love the concept of the app but wasn’t the best for me because I don’t charge my phone while I sleep and don’t have constant access to a charger throughout my day. 

I charge my phone in the evening before sleep and for an hour before work and usually this is plenty for me. Was at 100% before going to sleep last night and usually with phone usage during the night I will start my morning with at least 80% charge. This morning it was at 20%. Charged my phone this morning before work to nearly full charge but it was below 10% by midday. Checked which apps are using the most battery and rise was using the vast majority despite me actually opening the app 3 times. 
I only recommend app if you have a charger next to where you sleep and have access while you work. Plenty of trackers out there that can tell you more about your sleep without taking away so much battery.

reviews.title: Great app but please offer monthly subscription option
reviews.contents: I love the app, particularly useful for tracking sleep/waking at night, but I wish there was an option for a monthly subscription - I paid the $5.99 for a 1 month trial, and came on looking to buy another month, but the only option for $85 for a year is too big of a commitment to justify. Would be great if there was an option for a monthly subscription (like $7 or $8) as I was finding it really interesting to see my sleep patterns over a few weeks and would have liked to use it for a few more months at least to see if I could improve my insomnia and increase my energy levels. The slow alarm is a great feature too.
